advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the local HEAD history reaches the fork point in real CI (or fetch the fork point via the explicit URL) so merge-base does not silently fall back to main's tip when origin is unavailable.
evidence: scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py:520: subprocess.run(["git", "fetch", "--unshallow"], ...) with no explicit URL, so it uses the default (origin) remote

Commit message and docstring for _fetch_base_ceilings_from_main state the lock fetches main by EXPLICIT URL precisely so it does NOT depend on an origin remote (scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py:545-548), yet the --unshallow deepening depends on that same default remote
scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py:533: `if merge_base.returncode != 0 or not rev:` falls back to main_ref (tip) — the exact comparison the change exists to avoid
advisory.finding: The merge-base can only be computed if the LOCAL HEAD's ancestry reaches the fork point; the fetch deepens only the fetched `gh-main-complexity-lock` ref, and `git fetch --unshallow` relies on a default remote (origin) that this module deliberately does not depend on elsewhere. In CI checkouts where HEAD lacks the fork-point commit and origin is unavailable, merge-base fails and the code silently falls back to main's tip — reintroducing the original false-positive behavior for that checkout.
scenarios: A GitHub Actions PR checkout that fetched only the PR ref (origin absent or non-fetchable) where HEAD's local history does not contain the merge base

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify CI checkouts that are not shallow still contain the fork point, or trigger deepening regardless of the shallow flag when merge-base initially fails.
evidence: scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py:509-517: deepening runs only when `--is-shallow-repository` returns exactly `"true"`
scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py:533: fallback to main_ref when no merge base is computable
advisory.finding: A non-shallow checkout that nonetheless lacks the fork-point commit (e.g. a single-branch PR checkout that is not marked shallow) skips deepening entirely, because deepening is gated only on `--is-shallow-repository == "true"`, then merge-base fails and falls back to tip.
scenarios: A PR checkout that is complete for its branch but does not carry main's fork-point commit and is not flagged shallow

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the full-history main fetch (dropping --depth=1) is an acceptable CI cost, or use a bounded --deepen/--shallow-since instead.
evidence: Diff comment at scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py:564-566 acknowledges the depth removal is intentional to enable merge-base computation
advisory.finding: Removing `--depth=1` makes the fetch pull main's full history rather than just its tip, which can materially increase CI fetch cost/time for large-history repositories.
scenarios: Every CI run of the lock gate on a repository with a long main history

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that exercises the shallow-repository -> `git fetch --unshallow` deepening path in `_base_commit_for_comparison`.
evidence: search of tests/unit/test_complexity_baseline.py for 'unshallow', 'shallow', 'is-shallow-repository' returned (no matches)
ABSENCE: no fixture creates a shallow repo (e.g. clone --depth=1) to drive the deepen path
advisory.finding: The shallow-repository deepening branch (git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository true -> git fetch --unshallow) added to _base_commit_for_comparison is untested; no test constructs a shallow checkout, so the branch that motivates dropping --depth=1 never executes under test.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test covering `_fetch_base_ceilings_from_main` end-to-end that asserts the merge-base rev (not main's tip) is the source of the ceilings read via cat-file/show.
evidence: search of tests/unit/test_complexity_baseline.py for '_fetch_base_ceilings_from_main', 'from_main', 'fetch', 'depth' returned (no matches)
ABSENCE: tests call ccb.parse_baseline on a hand-run `git show`, never the function under change that wires rev into the lookup
advisory.finding: _fetch_base_ceilings_from_main — the integration point where the merge-base rev is threaded into `git cat-file`/`git show` and where `--depth=1` was removed — has no test. The forked_repo tests reconstruct the `git show <rev>:baseline` step by hand rather than calling _fetch_base_ceilings_from_main, so a regression that re-uses `ref` (main's tip) instead of `rev` (the merge base) at lines 580/588 would not be detected by the new tests.
